learning_outcomes.text: Applies manufacturing, metrology, and quality control systems and processes. Applies materials engineering to manufacturing processes.
Applies experimental techniques to manufacturing processes.
Understands the principles of manufacturing metal elements, casting, machining, and plastic deformation.
Evaluates the suitability of different materials and their implications in manufacturing processes. Identifies changes in material properties due to production processes.
Programs numerical control systems. Plans and tests different metal welding systems. Plans and executes metrology operations.

Intervenes effectively and transmits relevant information, appropriate to the situation. Plans communication: generates ideas, seeks information, selects and orders information, creates outlines, determines audience type, communication objectives, ... Drafts documents with appropriate format, content, structure, linguistic correctness, register, and illustrates concepts using conventions correctly: formats, titles, captions, legends, ... Their presentations are properly prepared, using strategies to present and deliver their oral presentations (audiovisual aids, gaze, voice, gesture, time control, ...).

Participates actively and shares information, knowledge, and experiences. Makes their individual contribution within the planned time and with available resources. Accepts and complies with group rules. Actively collaborates in team work planning, task distribution, and required deadlines.

Collects significant information needed to solve problems based on objective criteria. Follows a logical method to identify problem causes. Presents different alternative solution options for the same problem and evaluates their possible risks and advantages. Develops a strategy to solve the problem. Obtains necessary support from others to achieve success in their decisions. Has the ability to lead the decision-making process participatively. Methodically questions new ways of doing things, seeks new procedures, and experiments with new procedures. Analyzes risks and benefits of innovation.

teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Introduction to the subject and explanation of its regulations.

Lecture session: Development of the theoretical content of the corresponding practical session and explanation of how the practical session will be carried out. Students must come to the laboratory with these contents assimilated to perform the practical session correctly.

Laboratory practices: In each practical session, in groups, the corresponding practical session will be carried out according to the script, and a report detailing the results and conclusions must be submitted. It is essential that the student comes with the report read and analyzed.
Personalized attention: Personalized attention will be provided to students who require it.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices: Completion of scripts in practices to be submitted on the same day. This grade also includes the procedure used in the practice and possible questions about the theory of the practice.
Oral tests: Individual oral test to be carried out at the end of the semester (all practices).
Mixed tests: Test 1: P1-P4. Test 2: P5-P7. Tests that may contain open-ended questions, short questions, and/or multiple-choice questions.
Objective short-answer tests: Pre- and/or post-practice self-assessments.

assessment_rules: For evaluation according to Scenario A, a minimum grade of 5 points is required in all evaluative elements: overall grade of Moodle tests, overall grade of practicals, grade of partial P1-P4, and grade of partial P5-P7. For evaluation according to Scenario B, a minimum grade of 4 points is required in the oral exam. To pass the subject, the minimum grade for the final oral exam must be equal to or greater than 4 points. There is no second call for this subject. Attendance to practices is mandatory, and only one unjustified absence is allowed. Failure to recover any practice within the established deadline directly implies failing the subject.
